assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a new concept of molecular organisation: membraneless compartments (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) behave as condensed phases governed by multivalency, thermodynamics and phase behaviour. This reduces a messy cellular phenomenon to general physical-chemical principles, which I value highly, and it connects to my own work on self-assembly, amyloid and non-equilibrium organisation.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne established the P-granule liquid-droplet picture in 2009; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work provided the quantitative phase-diagram framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence-encoded theory and disordered-protein physics but a three-person prize is cleanest with these three, as I recall the history (not independently verified).
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and highly influential, with rapid uptake across cell biology, biophysics and disease. Some timing risk because the field is still debating in-cell stoichiometry, material states and which condensates are functionally relevant, so the claim may be strongest as a general principle rather than for every example.
uncertainties: Debate over whether many reported condensates are physiologically relevant versus in vitro or overexpression artefacts.
Whether chemistry, as opposed to physiology, is the natural home of the prize.
Credit split between experimental discovery and theory (Pappu, Mittag) is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and phase-behaviour story: pH-dependent charge, non-bilayer lipid phases and controlled encapsulation made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, with enormous societal and scientific impact (mRNA vaccines, siRNA therapy). As a lipid physical chemist I see this as colloid and membrane chemistry applied with real rigour.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) built the lipid-vesicle and encapsulation foundation; ionizable-lipid optimisation involved MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, among others. The decisive ones are contested and a clean three-person split is difficult. I propose the foundational formulation chemists but acknowledge competing claims.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale, so maturity is high; recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize already honoured the mRNA modification side, which may affect committee appetite.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and with the nucleoside-modification discovery.
Allocation among Cullis group, Acuitas/Arbutus lipid chemists and Anderson/Langer lipidoids is unclear.
Whether it counts as discovery of new chemistry or enabling formulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory (funnels, frustration, hydrophobic-collapse and folding thermodynamics) gave a general physical-chemical framework for protein folding and shaped the later era of structure prediction and biomolecular simulation. It is a clear example of thermodynamic reasoning unifying a complex biological process.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are most associated with funnel landscape theory and minimal frustration, Dill with the hydrophobic-collapse/lattice-model framework; Bryngelson and Fersht made important theoretical and experimental contributions. A theory-focused trio is plausible but others have credible claims.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental support (kinetics, single-molecule, simulations) and conceptual acceptance. The prize may be considered partly overtaken by the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design, which weakens urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize for computational protein design and structure prediction.
Relative weighting of theory versus Fersht's experimental mapping.
Difficulty in selecting three among several pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-liquid-crystal templating of mesoporous silica is a direct use of self-assembly and phase behaviour to build ordered porous solids with tunable pore size, opening a field in catalysis, adsorption and nanoscience. It established that amphiphile mesophases can template inorganic matter, a concept I find intellectually clean.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil team (Kresge, Beck and co-workers) discovered MCM-41; Stucky's group (with Zhao) extended the approach to SBA-15 and broader mechanistic understanding; Ryoo and Inagaki had parallel contributions. Attribution is plausible for three but with real competing claims, including the Japanese FSM-16 work.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature for 30 years, with widespread use, though practical impact is moderate compared with other candidates and the timing has long passed any initial window.
uncertainties: Competing independent discovery claims (FSM-16 versus MCM-41).
Practical industrial impact has been narrower than early expectations.
Whether the Mobil patents-and-papers credit is cleanly attributed to named individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coordination-driven self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules showed that thermodynamically controlled, reversible metal-ligand bonding yields complex three-dimensional architectures in high yield, with host-guest chemistry and confined catalysis. It is a significant concept in molecular organisation.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (first discrete coordination cages and encapsulation), Raymond (tetrahedral and other supramolecular hosts, confined reactivity) and Nitschke (subcomponent self-assembly) are strong; Stang's molecular-library work is also major. This is a crowded field already honoured in 1987 and 2016.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with widespread independent confirmation and ongoing application development; the main question is whether the field has had enough transformative uses beyond host-guest chemistry.
uncertainties: Proximity to prior supramolecular and molecular-machine prizes.
Choice among Fujita, Raymond, Stang and Nitschke is difficult.
Limited large-scale application so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography are classic surface and colloid chemistry: spontaneous organisation of amphiphiles on surfaces gave molecular-level control of interfacial properties, with consequences for biosensing, microfluidics and nanofabrication.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiol and disulfide monolayers on gold in 1983, Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are important precedent, and Whitesides developed the broad systematic chemistry and soft lithography. Priority and attribution among these is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely used, with decades of confirmation; the question is whether the moment has passed.
uncertainties: Priority dispute and role of Sagiv and Xia.
Soft lithography is a technique distinct from monolayer chemistry; they might need separate recognition.
Age and availability of laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing converts single-molecule passage through a pore into an electrical signal and has produced sequencing devices in wide use. The underlying biophysical and membrane-protein engineering ideas are elegant and relevant to my interest in membranes and interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon and Deamer demonstrated nucleic-acid translocation, Branton and Deamer conceived DNA sequencing through pores, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled readout. The distribution of credit is complicated and a three-person selection omits important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercial and validated, but the broader impact for chemistry beyond sequencing is still developing, and recognition could be considered timely or slightly premature.
uncertainties: Several essential contributions would be omitted by a three-person limit.
Impact is concentrated in sequencing, which overlaps with other biochemistry recognition.
Whether the prize would emphasise chemistry or technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation using PROTACs and molecular glues reframes small-molecule pharmacology as proximity-induced chemistry, with the first clinical molecules now in trials. The idea is conceptually new and has high potential impact in medicinal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced PROTACs, Ciulli contributed structure-guided small-molecule E3 ligase recruitment (VHL ligands), and Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. The glue arm may deserve separate credit, complicating a clean trio.
assessment.maturity: Promising but still maturing: clinical validation is incomplete and long-term impact is not yet established, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical proof of concept is still emerging.
Compound discovery: PROTAC concept and molecular-glue mechanism could require distinct allocation.
Lower direct overlap with my own expertise, so I weigh it with less confidence.
